work.name: Walmart
work.summary: Developed multi-model regression ensemble for transportation optimization.
highlights: Built ensemble model (XGBoost, RF, Extra Trees, LightGBM, Prophet, ARIMA) to optimize outbound shipments with 85%+ accuracy, beating production model by 3%.
Projected $1M ARR savings by streamlining 15,000 weekly load forecasts, cutting empty miles and variance.
Cleaned and joined item/routing data in SQL; evaluated demand signals with confidence intervals and variance analysis.
Collaborated in Agile/Jira setup, participating in sprint planning, stand-ups, and one-on-ones with manager.

work.name: University of Florida Statistics Department
highlights: Reinforced regression, chi-square, and ANOVA through office hours and review sessions.
Developed exams and assignments emphasizing applied stats concepts.

work.name: Nettles Lab at UF Scripps Institute
work.summary: Built self-supervised autoencoder pipeline for hormone-sensitive cancer datasets.
highlights: Applied dimensionality reduction and clustering to study treatment effects.
Used normalization, decorrelation, and cross-validation to improve model reliability.
Optimized model performance to analyze steroid hormone receptor structures.

work.name: UF Health Outcomes and Biomedical Informatics
work.summary: Researched protein–peptide binding and hypertensive disorder detection under Dr. Dominick Lemas.
highlights: Developed CNN for protein–peptide binding prediction rivaling AlphaFold.
Built PyTorch NN on EHR data to detect hypertensive disorders with 96.5% accuracy.
Analyzed 600,000+ EHRs, creating a data dictionary for obesity and hypertension impacts.
